title: Investigating Evaluator Anchoring: Does the Order Models Are Presented Affect Safety Rankings?
original_idea: Submit the same model outputs to an LLM judge in randomized orders across ten evaluation runs. Compute whether safety score variance correlates with position in the evaluation queue.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Related to position bias (gen-0666) but for sequential batch evaluation. Incremental extension of known bias. Moderate impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Randomize order, run LLM judge ten times, compute statistics. Straightforward experimental design. API calls and basic statistics. Accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Same outputs, ten randomized runs, correlation analysis. Very well-bounded and completable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: 'Judging the Judges: A Systematic Study of Position Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge' (arXiv:2406.07791, IJCNLP 2025) directly studies position bias in LLM evaluation and found approximately 40% inconsistency in GPT-4 evaluations due to position effects. 'Justice or Prejudice? Quantifying Biases in LLM-as-a-Judge' (2024) systematically quantifies position bias, verbosity bias, self-enhancement bias, and other evaluation biases. Mitigation strategies including order randomization and majority voting among heterogeneous judges are well-documented. The proposed experiment (same outputs, ten randomized runs, correlation with queue position) is a strict subset of the position bias analyses already published. The safety-specific framing adds minimal novelty since the bias mechanism is domain-independent.
